newsitem.title: USA: Republicans urge more East Europe NATO members.
newsitem.headline: Republicans urge more East Europe NATO members.

text.p: Senior House of Representatives Republicans introduced a bill on Thursday urging NATO membership for Romania, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania as soon as they meet membership requirements.

The bill would also declare U.S. policy against NATO's pledge not to station nuclear weapons or NATO troops in the new members' territory but would support other efforts to show Russia that NATO enlargement is not a threat.
It would require Defence Secretary William Cohen to seek cooperation with Russia on anti-missile defence projects.

House Republicans including Majority Leader Dick Armey and International Relations Committee Chairman Benjamin Gilman announced the bill at a news conference. They said they believed NATO in July would invite Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovenia to become NATO members and were introducing the bill to assure other East European countries they were in line for membership later.

"It is critical that such countries not be left in any security vacuum," Gilman, a New York Republican, said. "These countries must be assured that they will not be forgotten; that the door to NATO will remain open to them."

A binding provision of the bill would require President Bill Clinton to seek NATO membership for such countries and provide aid to help them meet military and democratic policy requirements for NATO membership.
The bill would also express the non-binding sense of Congress that Romania, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania specifically be invited to be NATO members.

It would declare that U.S. policy supports a NATO-Russia charter and new concessions to Russia in the 1990 Conventional Armed Forces in Europe Treaty to show that NATO enlargement is no threat to Russia.

But the policy would oppose concessions to Russia that treat new members differently than present ones, including a NATO pledge to Russia that it has no plan to station nuclear weapons or NATO troops in the East European member countries.

The bill would require Cohen to seek U.S.-Russian creation of a joint global warning centre to detect and report any launch of missiles by one country against another, and to conduct U.S.-Russian anti-missile defence exercises.
